shots.phrase: Begin by framing Course Foundations and Scope as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.

Topics include the knowledge discovery process; data exploration and its role; data extraction, cleaning, integration and transformation; handling numeric, unstructured, text, web, and other forms of data; and ethical issues underlying data preparation and mining.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Data Exploration and Its Role precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate how exploratory data analysis reveals missing values and outliers in a sample dataset.
A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
With the foundation in place, examine how Data Extraction and Cleaning operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: Students will practice extracting structured data from a CSV file and removing duplicate rows using standard cleaning techniques.
The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
Next, compare the choices involved in Data Integration and Transformation and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate merging two relational tables and converting categorical variables into numeric codes.
Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
Apply Handling Numeric Data to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
This course provides an introduction to the concepts and techniques used in preparing data for subsequent data mining.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Handling Unstructured and Text Data, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate converting a paragraph of text into a list of tokens and removing common stop words.
Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
Stress-test the reasoning around Handling Web Data with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Relational systems organize data with tables, rows, columns, and declared types.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Data Integrity and Constraints to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Consider this worked case: Instructor will demonstrate how primary keys and foreign keys prevent duplicate and orphaned records in a relational database.
The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
Connect Ethical Issues in Data Preparation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: Students will review a case study on anonymizing personal data and ensuring fair representation in cleaned datasets.
The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Consider this worked case: Students will complete a checklist verifying extraction accuracy, cleaning completeness, transformation consistency, and ethical compliance.
The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
